options.help: The game's own console profile. Series S is its low preset (smaller textures, lower detail, 1080p); Series X its high one (2160p).
options.cost: Series S is about 2-3x faster than Series X

options.help: The screen size the game is told the console is plugged into (WxH, 640x360 to 7680x4320). The game picks its output and render size from it.
options.cost: Cost grows with the pixel count: 1440p is 1.8x and 2160p 4x the pixels of 1080p

options.help: Which graphics card to use on a PC with more than one: part of its name (5060) or #index. Empty: Windows' default card.
Shrinks the game's window to at most WxH (keeps aspect, centred). The picture is stretched: softer, same frame rate. Not a render-resolution setting.
Game-side: the fraction of the output height the game renders at before its own upscaler (0.2 to 1.0; the hook cannot go above native).
options.cost: Lower is much faster and softer

options.help: Game-side: forces the game's own temporal upscaler on (the console profile Series S needs it at any scale below 1).
options.cost: Small cost, hides the lower render scale

options.help: Which screen the game's window opens on: part of the monitor's name (Alienware), DISPLAY1, #index (0 is the first output) or primary. Empty: the primary screen. The log lists every screen at start.
A borderless window the size of the chosen screen instead of a small window (the picture is stretched to it).
options.cost: A bigger window costs a little GPU time

options.help: auto: HDR output when Windows HDR is on for the chosen screen (turn on Use HDR for it in Windows Settings; VIctory never changes that). on: always tell the game HDR is available and present PQ/BT.2020. off: SDR. stretch: APPROXIMATION, the game stays SDR and its picture is expanded to HDR.
HDR only: the brightness in nits of SDR white (the interface, menus and the numbers panel; default 200). The game's own HDR picture is not changed by it.
Rays end at the root (miss) while the structure builder is off. Off: the title's ray walks run and may hang on stale structures.
options.cost: On is faster and avoids hangs; off needs the structure builder (not available on NVIDIA)

options.help: list: skip the ~1,034 ray-tracing resolve and traced-shadow shaders of scripts/rt_off_hashes.txt (diagnostics build only). none: run them.
options.cost: list saves GPU time; the skipped passes give less bounced light

options.help: Stand-in for the indirect light the rays would give: this share of an estimate worked out from the frame (0 or off: the title's own, black indoors). Also constant:<level>.
Bound for the light the air scatters, as a multiple of the light around (0: the title's own). Lower removes brown fog veils indoors.
How many times the estimate the title's own light may keep (4 when unset). Lower stops rooms by a window from glowing.
Crease shading of the stand-in: <strength>,<radius in metres> (default 1,0.6).
A NaN a shader writes is made 0 before blur and upscaler spread it: removes black blobs. Baked into translated shaders.
Texture residency policy: auto = the new budgeted policy (floor, reserve, eviction); legacy = the base's rule.
options.cost: auto keeps more detail resident within the card's budget

options.help: Hard cap on host texture copies in MB (legacy residency only). Empty: derived from the card's budget.
options.cost: Higher is sharper but risks spilling card memory into PC RAM (stutter)

options.help: Top mips of a host copy bigger than this are dropped (0: none; empty: the build's default: 8-64 MB by card at 7c0cdf6, off at 28d8475 because a cap banded the picture). Higher keeps more close-up detail.
options.cost: Higher costs video memory (and can spill into PC RAM on small cards); lower fits small cards

options.help: Memory the residency policy keeps free for everything else.
options.cost: Higher is safer, textures get less room

options.help: Texture bytes always admitted whatever the memory use.
options.cost: Higher keeps more detail under pressure

options.help: Texture MB staged to the card per frame under the new policy (automatic: 48-192 MB by card).
options.cost: Higher fills textures faster, longer frames

options.help: Texture MB uploaded per frame (empty: automatic). Higher drains the first minutes of black surfaces sooner.
Whether texture refreshes wait for the title's memory to hold still. wait: correct skin/materials; no-wait: faster, can show rainbow skin.
Upload textures ahead of the draw lists that use them (less pop-in).
Relay stage for the title's copies. 1: correct bodies (no stretched or jumping characters); 2: faster.
options.cost: Stage 1 costs about 7 fps with card steps 0

options.help: Card-side steps of the relay. 0: correct bodies; 2: fastest.
options.cost: 0 costs the submitting thread about 30 ms a frame

options.help: Milliseconds a frame may wait for new shader pipelines to compile instead of skipping their draws (default 500). Higher: fewer missing objects, longer first-time hitches.
options.cost: Only costs time the first time a place is seen

options.help: Descriptor slots for dynamic views. Too few drops draws (missing objects) on cards capped at 1,000,000.
Video memory for card-side copies of the title's buffers (memory compares on the card, not the CPU: about 2x fps on Series S).
options.cost: Larger is faster until memory runs out

options.help: Zero-copy memory on integrated or unified-memory GPUs.
Legacy residency only: the share of card memory textures may fill (default 90).
options.cost: Higher keeps more textures, risks spilling into PC RAM

options.help: keep: idle texture copies stay up to 10 minutes while memory is free; release-early: dropped after 5 s.
Copies of textures are made level by level on demand (needs tiled-resources tier 2). Saves memory.
Threads that map the title's memory (empty: 8).
options.cost: More can help streaming, costs CPU

options.help: Threads that compile shader pipelines (empty: two thirds of the cores).
options.cost: More shortens first-time hitches, takes CPU from the game

options.help: Keep the ~1,000 ray-tracing resolve shaders instead of leaving them out while the structure builder is off.
options.cost: Costs GPU time; the light they give is wrong without structures

options.help: EXPERIMENTAL: builds the ray-tracing structures. Cannot run on NVIDIA cards (64-lane programs refused).
Exact half-float rounding in translated shaders. Baked into shaders: the first run re-translates everything.
Shows the numbers panel (F3 toggles). F8 opens the quality page whether or not this is on.
Scoped timers and a stall report at the end of the run.
GPU timestamps per pass for the numbers panel and profile.
